I have spent a fair amount of seconds milling this idea around in my head since the rule and have canceled a few comments before posting them. I keep getting stuck trying to reconcile this concept of /v/all being the stream of all the site content like we expect it to be vs. subs being able to set themselves private vs. subs requiring a minimum contribution before downvoating vs. restricting new users' voting powers. I think what I'm struggling with more or less the following:

  1. Subs could already set themselves as private. Unlike on other sites, this seems to only mean they don't show up in /v/all (as opposed to being locked down completely). However, if you know of the sub, you can at least access it as a reader (i.e. posting can also be restricted to approved users).
  2. Adding a non-zero CCP minimum effectively accomplishes step 1. However, in spite of the potential (and evidence) of abuse, if we step back and take a broad view of the idea behind the implementation of this, it seems to me it was never intended be a method of excluding the entire sub from the general population of the site. In other words, this reeks of feature creep. How did we not foresee that some mods were going to set their CCP minimum to some absurdly high number back when this was implemented?
  3. CCP minimum isn't meant (AFAIK) to make your sub private as much as it's meant to impose a minimum level of participation before users can bury content.

While keeping in mind that the site is in alpha, features like these can always come and go. I really liked that "private" subs only basically meant they were excluded from all and not that they were locked down. This new feature in effect renders the private feature redundant, among other things.

The first thing I thought when this new feature was implemented was that it seemed as if we were conflating /v/all with our personal front pages. Yes, with a new site and relatively small userbase, browsing /v/all is a really good idea, but the primary entry point for the site is still a front page of subs you choose to subscribe to. It doesn't seem like the best way to prevent asshats from upvoat-brigading shitposts is to tell non-troll mods that if they want to require users to participate a little before downvoating they must also exclude their subs form /v/all when the reality of it is that only a small proportion of mods engage in this shitty behavior much the same way only a small proportion of normal users will be real trolls. And in case what I'm implying is a little too subtle, this idea of "even playing field" is a little bullshitty too, since we have mods and already restrict new users from full voting access. This is all a little too knee-jerky and reactionary for my taste.

Sorry if this seemed a little ranty. I love you @Atko.
